title: Finite, integral and rational derived operations with normalized scalar comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$
[def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and
uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and for $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].
Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; for $W\in\{X,Y\}$ and a ring $A$, $A_W$ is the
constant coefficient sheaf and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the derived category of
$A_W$-modules. Let $f^{-1}$ be the inverse image of pro-etale sheaves along $f$
[def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. At finite level $A=A_{E,n}$, use the canonical ring-sheaf
isomorphism $c^f_A:f^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$
[prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] and the exact module pullback
[prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Here $f_n$ denotes $f$ regarded as the
morphism of ringed sites
$(X_{\mathrm{proet}},(A_{E,n})_X)\to(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(A_{E,n})_Y)$.

**Finite level.** Put $A=A_{E,n}$. For $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $W\in\{X,Y\}$
and $M,N\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ define

$$
 Lf_n^*K=L(f_n)^*K=f^{-1}K\otimes^L_{f^{-1}A_Y}A_X,
 \qquad
 M\otimes_A^L N,
 \qquad
 R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N):
$$

the first is the derived module pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations],
computed with a K-flat resolution; since the module inverse image is exact and
$c^f_A$ is an isomorphism, it is represented by $f^{-1}$ applied termwise to
any representative of $K$, with its module action transported along $c^f_A$.
The second is the derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor], computed
with a K-flat resolution of $M$. Its canonical independence of the resolution
is [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent], and its action on pairs
of morphisms is [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial]. The third is the derived internal Hom
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom] of the ringed site $(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A_W)$,
computed with a K-injective resolution of $N$. These are functors on the
ambient categories $D(-_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$; which of them preserve the
constructible subcategories $D^b_c(-,A_{E,n})$
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] is not part of this definition.

**Integral level** ($\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$). Here $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$
and $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ for $W\in\{X,Y\}$. On the derived-complete integral
categories $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
full subcategories of the derived category $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ of
modules over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $Lf^*$,
$\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}$ and $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}$ are the integral
derived operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]: the derived inverse
limits

$$
 Lf^*K=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nLf_n^*\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr),
 \qquad
 M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n
 \bigl((M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\bigr)
$$

of the compatible finite reductions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction],
and the derived internal Hom of $(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W})$. The K-flat and
K-injective resolutions are taken in the ambient category of
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$-modules; a resolution is not required to remain in
$D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ term by term. In the displayed inverse limits, choose K-flat representatives
with flat terms and take all reductions of the same representative; the
transition maps and the functorial shifted-cone-of-$1-s$ construction are
those of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Its descent and independence
of resolutions are [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Thus the
notation denotes that construction, whose values satisfy the derived-limit
triangle [def-weil-derived-limit], rather than an unspecified choice of a
triangle separately for each object. By
[lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], $Lf^*$ carries
$D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and
$\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}$ carries $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)^2$ into
$D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$. The internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}(M,N)$ is
taken as an operation of $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ only for the pairs $M,N$ for
which it lies in $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$.

**Rational level** ($\Lambda=E$). On
$D^b_c(W,E)=D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
whose objects are those of $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, use the integral
operations on objects. On morphisms extend the integral maps linearly in
each variable. Explicitly, for integral morphisms $u:K\to K'$, $v:M\to M'$,
$w:N\to N'$ and $c,d\in E$ set

$$
 Lf_E^*(u\otimes c)=Lf^*(u)\otimes c,\qquad
 (v\otimes c)\otimes^L_E(w\otimes d)
 =(v\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}w)\otimes cd.
$$

For $a:M'\to M$, $b:N\to N'$ integral, define

$$
 R\mathcal Hom_E(a\otimes c,b\otimes d)
 =R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}(a,b)\otimes cd.
$$

The last formula has source $R\mathcal Hom_E(M,N)$ and target
$R\mathcal Hom_E(M',N')$ and is used on the full subcategory of pairs with
constructible integral internal Hom. These formulas extend additively to
sums of pure tensors; the integral maps are $\mathcal O_E$-linear in each
variable, so the tensor-product balancing relation is respected. Write
$Lf_E^*$, $\otimes^L_E$, $R\mathcal Hom_E$ for these operations.


For a coefficient inclusion E → L, use the integral scalar-extension comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Their rationalizations give the uniquely normalized pullback and tensor scalar comparisons; on integral representatives they are the localized prescribed integral comparisons. Scalar extension sends every permitted internal-Hom pair to a permitted pair, and the internal-Hom scalar comparison is uniquely normalized by its localized integral component. No common-stage quotient construction is asserted by this node.

source.place: The finite, integral and rational paragraphs, and rationalization of the scalar comparisons in the common-stage paragraph; extraction of already proved constructions only

proof.text: Use the existing intrinsic finite inverse image, finite closed structure, K-flat models and quotient evaluation calculus. The definitions are the identical finite declarations formerly in DerivedPullbackTensorHom, with positive exponent n+1.

Restrict the actual integral pullback and completed tensor to constructible objects with the existing preservation theorem. Restrict internal Hom only to the full subcategory of pairs satisfying the constructibility predicate.

For rational pullback use normalized additive scalar localization of the integral linear functor. For rational tensor use the existing bilinear scalar-localization theorem. For rational internal Hom use permitted contravariant bilinear localization. Integral linearity and bilinearity supply the required Hom maps and normalization formulas. Unique-existence specifications determine each chosen functor.

Restrict the prescribed integral scalar comparisons, verify naturality by the integral squares, and apply normalized unary and semilinear bilinear localization comparisons. For permitted Hom pairs, transport the constructibility predicate using the actual scalar Hom isomorphism and conjugate the localized integral comparison by the fixed object equalities. Component extensionality gives uniqueness.

theorem rationalDerivedInternalHom_existsUnique (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (W : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃! F : (constructibleRationalHomPairs l E W).FullSubcategory ⥤
        sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E W,
      (∀ P, F.obj P = ⟨(constructibleIntegralHom l E W).obj
        (integralPairOfRationalHomPair l E W P)⟩) ∧
      (∀ (P Q : (constructibleRationalHomPairs l E W).FullSubcategory),
        ∃ b : (Q.obj.1.unop ⟶ P.obj.1.unop)
          →ₗ[Localization.Away (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)]
          (P.obj.2 ⟶ Q.obj.2)
          →ₗ[Localization.Away (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)]
          (F.obj P ⟶ F.obj Q),
        (∀ a b', F.map (ObjectProperty.homMk (Prod.mkHom a.op b')) = b a b') ∧
        ∀ (a : Q.obj.1.unop.obj ⟶ P.obj.1.unop.obj)
          (b' : P.obj.2.obj ⟶ Q.obj.2.obj)
          (c d : Localization.Away (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)),
          HEq (b (c ⊗ₜ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E] a)
            (d ⊗ₜ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E] b'))
            ((c * d) ⊗ₜ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E]
              (constructibleIntegralHom l E W).map
                (X := integralPairOfRationalHomPair l E W P)
                (Y := integralPairOfRationalHomPair l E W Q)
                (ObjectProperty.homMk (Prod.mkHom a.op b'))))
